rule: LGA must be one of the 4 codes in lgas.csv
prevents: enumerator entering a non-existent LGA code

rule: Ward must be one of wards.csv filtered to selected LGA (lga_code = ${lga})
prevents: ward/LGA mismatches; ward chosen outside the assigned LGA

rule: Settlement must be one of settlements.csv filtered to selected ward (ward_code = ${ward})
prevents: settlement/ward mismatches; unusable 2500-row list on device
source: settlements.csv (data pack) + judgement on cascade design

rule: Enumerator code must exist in staff_roster.csv with role = Enumerator
prevents: recording a non-existent or wrongly-typed enumerator code

rule: Team code auto-filled from staff_roster.csv based on enumerator code (team_code column)
prevents: team code disagreeing with the enumerator's actual team
source: staff_roster.csv (data pack) + judgement (avoid re-asking a value the roster already fixes)

rule: Date of visit must fall within the fieldwork window (1-30 June 2026 per form header)
prevents: dates outside the fieldwork period being recorded as valid

rule: GPS reading compared against selected settlement's registered lat/long (settlements.csv/geojson); flagged not blocked if far outside expected range
prevents: silently accepting a GPS fix from the wrong location
source: settlements.csv/geojson (data pack) + judgement (soft check only; dwellings aren't at centroid)

rule: If 1.12 = 2 (No) or 8 (Do not know), skip to 1.14
prevents: enumerator completing 1.13 when there is no prior-round household to reference

rule: If shown, household id must exist in previous_round_households.csv
prevents: recording a prior-round id that doesn't exist in the register

rule: If 1.14 in {2,3,4}, form ends; no further sections rendered
prevents: enumerator continuing to Sections 2+ on a non-completed visit

rule: If 2.02 = 2 (Consent refused), form ends; no further sections rendered
prevents: enumerator continuing the interview without consent
household size of 0 or an implausibly large number being accepted
source: judgement (no stated range on paper; 30 chosen as a generous upper bound for a household survey
column6: flagged as judgement not a hard demographic ceiling)

rule: Number of roster rows actually completed must equal the value entered at 3.01
prevents: household size stated but roster under- or over-filled relative to that count
source: questionnaire requirement (assessment explicitly requires reconciling stated household size against the roster)

rule: Value at 3.02 must equal count of roster rows where column (7) = eligible (age 9-59 completed months)
prevents: enumerator manually miscounting eligible children instead of the system deriving it
source: questionnaire logic (column 7 is marked "office use" on paper; digitised form can compute this instead of relying on a clerk)

prevents: enumerator opening Section 4 with zero eligible children

rule: Number of Section 4 modules completed must equal the value entered at 3.02
prevents: fewer or more child modules completed than the stated eligible count
source: questionnaire requirement (assessment explicitly requires reconciling eligible children count against completed child modules)
